phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Watch this bird off trap B.
phrases.meaning: 'Bird' is a target, not a real bird; trap B is the machine marked B.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Today we walk the Sporting course, tomorrow it's Compak.
phrases.meaning: Two different disciplines on two different days.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Point it, don't aim it.
phrases.meaning: A shotgun is swung and pointed with both eyes on the target, not aimed like a rifle.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: That's a CPSA term — under FITASC it's a simultaneous double.
phrases.meaning: The coach switches from British vocabulary to the FITASC name.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Ask the chief referee, not the stand referee.
phrases.meaning: The question is for the senior official of the competition.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: The jury will decide this one.
phrases.meaning: The matter goes beyond the stand referee, to the competition jury.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Guns open and empty between stands, please.
phrases.meaning: Walking to the next stand, the gun is broken with no cartridges inside.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Break your gun and show me it’s clear.
phrases.meaning: Open the gun (not damage it!) so I can see the chambers are empty.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Don’t load until you’re on the stand and I say so.
phrases.meaning: No cartridges in the gun while walking or waiting.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Muzzles down when you turn round.
phrases.meaning: Never let the barrels point at people, even with an open gun.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Stop! Stop! Guns open!
phrases.meaning: Emergency stop: stop shooting, open the gun, wait.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Eyes and ears on before you leave the clubhouse.
phrases.meaning: Put on glasses and hearing protection before walking out to the layouts.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Where are your ears?
phrases.meaning: “Ears” = hearing protection, not the ears themselves.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You can’t shoot in sandals here.
phrases.meaning: Closed shoes are required for safety.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Your number’s folded — it has to be fully visible.
phrases.meaning: The competitor number on the back must be complete and visible; otherwise a warning.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Quiet behind, please — she’s on.
phrases.meaning: The shooter is on the stand; everyone stops talking.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Wait until he’s opened his gun.
phrases.meaning: Nobody talks or moves until the shooter has finished and opened the gun.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Stand right behind me so you can see what I see.
phrases.meaning: In training the coach wants you directly behind, out of the swing.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Keep out of his line, please.
phrases.meaning: You are in the shooter’s view or near the barrels’ path; move back.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Number twelve — last call!
phrases.meaning: The referee is calling a missing shooter; if he does not come, his targets will be zeros.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: You’re next — get ready.
phrases.meaning: Prepare now: glasses, ears, cartridges, but do not step up until the stand is free.

phrases.speaker: shooter
phrases.en: Well shot!
phrases.meaning: Sincere praise after a good target or stand.

phrases.speaker: shooter
phrases.en: Bad luck.
phrases.meaning: Friendly sympathy after a miss, not criticism.

phrases.speaker: shooter
phrases.en: Thanks, ref — thanks for pulling.
phrases.meaning: Thanking the referee and the trapper at the end of the round.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Bring your over-and-under and a spare set of chokes.
phrases.meaning: The two-barrel competition gun plus extra choke tubes.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: With a semi-auto, keep the bolt open until you're on the stand.
phrases.meaning: Safety rule: a semi-automatic is carried with the breech open.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: No pumps on this ground.
phrases.meaning: Pump-action guns are not accepted.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You're seeing too much rib — your head is up.
phrases.meaning: The eye is too high above the rib, usually because the head lifts off the comb.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Check your selector — you fired the top barrel first.
phrases.meaning: The barrel selector is set the wrong way round.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Break your gun and show me it's clear.
phrases.meaning: Open the gun and show empty chambers.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Forget the bead — look at the target.
phrases.meaning: Focus on the target, not on the end of the barrel.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: What chokes are you using? — Quarter and half.
phrases.meaning: Improved cylinder in one barrel, modified in the other.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Put quarter in the bottom and half in the top — the second bird is longer.
phrases.meaning: More open choke for the first, closer target; tighter for the second, farther one.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Open up — these are all close.
phrases.meaning: Fit more open chokes because the targets are near.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Check your tubes are tight before the round.
phrases.meaning: Make sure the choke tubes have not loosened.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Empties in the bin, please, not on the grass.
phrases.meaning: Put fired hulls into the container.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Steel only on this ground.
phrases.meaning: Lead shot is not allowed on this ground (a local rule, not a FITASC one).

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Maximum twenty-eight grams on this shoot.
phrases.meaning: The load limit of the competition, as in the FITASC rules.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Nines for the close stuff, seven-and-a-halfs for the long crossers.
phrases.meaning: Finer No. 9 shot for near targets, larger No. 7½ for far crossing targets.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: The midi looks far but it isn't — don't give it too much.
phrases.meaning: The coach's correction for this target: it looks further away than it is, so this shooter is giving it more lead (more distance in front) than it needs. It is a correction for this situation, not a general rule.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: The battue will turn and drop at the end — take it when it shows its belly.
phrases.meaning: Shoot the battue once it turns its flat face towards you.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: The mini is dying fast — shoot it early.
phrases.meaning: The small target loses speed quickly; do not wait.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: The rabbit will hop on that bump — stay under it.
phrases.meaning: Keep the gun pointed low on the rolling target, so that if it hops up it jumps into the shot.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: The black one is the midi, the orange one is the standard — don't mix them up.
phrases.meaning: Two targets on the stand differ in colour and size.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You lose it against the trees — pick it up later, in the sky.
phrases.meaning: The target is hard to see in front of trees; start watching where the sky is behind it.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Flat light today — put the yellow lens in.
phrases.meaning: Grey light with little contrast; a yellow lens makes the target stand out more.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Trap B is throwing lower than in the showing — tell the referee.
phrases.meaning: The machine's trajectory has changed; the shooter should report it before shooting.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: It's voice release here — don't chat on the stand.
phrases.meaning: A microphone releases targets; talking can launch one.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: The trapper was late on that one — that's a no bird.
phrases.meaning: The target left more than three seconds after the call.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Layout three is the hard one today — lots of minis in the trees.
phrases.meaning: On the third layout there are many small targets flying through trees.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: On this stand, read the menu before you step in.
phrases.meaning: Check the order of traps and special targets first.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Stand two is a class C target, don't worry about it.
phrases.meaning: The target is graded as hard; a miss is expected.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Singles first, then doubles.
phrases.meaning: The standard order at every stand.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Read the menu: the traps go A, B, C.
phrases.meaning: The menu board lists the traps in the order they will be shot.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Next shooter.
phrases.meaning: The referee calls the next person onto the stand.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Check your score before you leave the stand.
phrases.meaning: Any disagreement must be raised now, not later.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Everybody move one to the right. Number five, to the waiting position.
phrases.meaning: The squad rotates; the shooter from station 5 goes behind station 1.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Trap E is the tower — it comes over your head.
phrases.meaning: The target from trap E is thrown from a high tower and passes overhead.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Mind the frame — don't swing past the post.
phrases.meaning: Respect the Firing Angle Limiter; do not swing the gun beyond it.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Move one station to the right.
phrases.meaning: Rotation after the shooter on station 5 has finished.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Gun open when you change stations.
phrases.meaning: Between stations the gun is open and unloaded.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Your double starts with the last target of the previous station.
phrases.meaning: The first target of your double is the same target that was shot last at the station before yours.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: You're waiting behind one.
phrases.meaning: The sixth shooter stands behind station 1.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Read the menu: on station three you have A, then F, then B, then the pair C and E on report.
phrases.meaning: Station 3: three singles, then a double on report; five targets in all.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Same traps, new menu — don't shoot from memory.
phrases.meaning: The order has changed since the last round.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Three singles, then a simo pair.
phrases.meaning: 'Simo' is short for a simultaneous double.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Long crosser, right to left — trust the lead and keep the gun moving.
phrases.meaning: The target is far away and flies from the shooter's right to left; give it the planned lead and do not stop the swing.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You're behind it — give it more.
phrases.meaning: The shot passed behind the target: more lead is needed.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: It's dropping at your break point — stay under the line.
phrases.meaning: Where the shooter breaks it, the crosser is already falling, so the gun must travel slightly below its path.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Pick it up early, it's quick off the trap.
phrases.meaning: Look for the target closer to the trap than usual, because it leaves the trap fast.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: The first one's quartering away to the left — take it quickly before it gets small.
phrases.meaning: The first target moves away at an angle to the shooter's left; break it early.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Quartering in from the right — don't let it get too close.
phrases.meaning: The target comes towards the shooter at an angle from the right; do not wait for it.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Less lead than you think — it's only a slight angle.
phrases.meaning: The target is nearly straight, so it needs only a small lead.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Take it out in front, before it gets on top of you.
phrases.meaning: Break the incomer while it is still in front, not when it is overhead.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Blot it out and keep swinging.
phrases.meaning: Let the barrels cover the target at the shot and do not stop the gun.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Don't wait on the going-away — it's getting smaller.
phrases.meaning: Shoot the going-away target promptly, because it is quickly getting further away.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: It comes from behind you — look back for it early.
phrases.meaning: It is an overhead from behind; turn the eyes towards it before calling.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Take the teal on the way up — keep the barrels moving above it.
phrases.meaning: Break the rising teal before the peak; the gun keeps rising past it.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Don't poke at it on the top.
phrases.meaning: Do not stop and aim at the target while it stalls at the peak.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: The looper's turning over — underneath and in front.
phrases.meaning: The target is rolling over the top of its arc and starting to fall; the lead goes below and ahead of it.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Second bird's dropping — go under it and keep the gun moving.
phrases.meaning: The second target of the pair is falling; shoot below it with the gun in motion.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: It hops on that bump — stay under it and keep moving.
phrases.meaning: The rabbit jumps at a known spot; keep the gun low and moving.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Shoot its feet.
phrases.meaning: Put the shot on the bottom edge of the rabbit, not over it.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: It slows down a lot — less lead than you think.
phrases.meaning: The rabbit loses speed quickly, so it needs a smaller lead.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Fur and feather: rabbit first, before it reaches the bushes.
phrases.meaning: In the rabbit-plus-bird pair, shoot the rabbit first because it disappears into cover.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: It's on report — finish the first one properly, the second waits for your shot.
phrases.meaning: The second target only comes when the shooter fires at the first, so there is no need to rush the first.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Simo: take the rabbit first, the teal will wait for you.
phrases.meaning: In the simultaneous pair shoot the rabbit first, because the teal stays in the air longer.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Rafale — after the first, come straight back to the trap for the second.
phrases.meaning: Both targets come from the same trap; after the first shot, return eyes and gun towards the trap to pick up the second.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: True pair from the tower, five of them.
phrases.meaning: Five simultaneous pairs thrown from the tower (English Sporting wording).

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Point your front foot at the break point.
phrases.meaning: Turn the toe of the front foot towards the place where the target will be broken.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Set your feet for the break, then wind back to the hold.
phrases.meaning: First place the feet for the break point, then turn the upper body back to the hold point.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Weight forward, soft knees.
phrases.meaning: Lean slightly onto the front foot and do not lock the knees.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Turn from the hips, not the arms.
phrases.meaning: The whole upper body rotates; the arms do not swing the gun on their own.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Gun to your face, not your face to the gun.
phrases.meaning: Lift the stock to the cheek; do not drop the head to meet the gun.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Muzzles first — move, mount, shoot.
phrases.meaning: Start the barrels moving with the target, mount during the move, fire as the mount is complete.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Your mount's late and too fast — start it with the front hand.
phrases.meaning: The gun comes up too late and with a jerk; the front hand should lead the movement earlier.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Low gun on this one, like in competition.
phrases.meaning: Start with the stock below the vest line, as the FITASC Sporting™ rules require.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Close your left eye as the gun comes up.
phrases.meaning: Shut the left eye during the mount, not before, so the right eye controls the gun.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Eyes on the clay, not the barrel.
phrases.meaning: Keep looking at the target; checking the barrel usually slows or stops the gun.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Look at the leading edge.
phrases.meaning: Focus on the front edge of the moving target, not its middle.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Don't look at the trap — look out to your pick-up point.
phrases.meaning: Wait with the eyes a little out along the line, where the target is first seen clearly.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Where are you taking it?
phrases.meaning: The coach asks where the shooter plans to break the target.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Move your hold point halfway back to the trap.
phrases.meaning: Hold the muzzles closer to the trap, at half of the current distance.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Look further out — pick it up where it's sharp.
phrases.meaning: Move the eyes away from the trap to where the target is first seen clearly.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Hold a little lower, just under the line.
phrases.meaning: Keep the muzzles slightly below the target's path at the call.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Follow through — the gun keeps moving after the bang.
phrases.meaning: Do not stop the swing at the shot.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You stopped the gun.
phrases.meaning: The muzzles stopped at the trigger, so the shot went behind.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Match the speed of the bird — you're racing it.
phrases.meaning: The gun is moving much faster than the target; move at the target's speed.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Slow the tempo down, this one gives you lots of time.
phrases.meaning: The target is slow or long, so the whole movement can be calmer.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Stay in the gun until you see it break.
phrases.meaning: Keep the cheek on the stock and eyes on the target until it breaks.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Forget the real distance — what matters is your picture.
phrases.meaning: Do not think in metres in the air; remember the gap you saw at the muzzle when you hit it.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: That's the picture — remember it.
phrases.meaning: The lead was right on that hit; keep the same sight picture.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Same lead on the right-to-left, it only looks different.
phrases.meaning: The real lead is equal in both directions; only perception changes.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Get in front and stay in front.
phrases.meaning: Put the muzzles ahead of the target and keep them there until after the shot.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Your insertion point is behind the bird — put the gun in front of it.
phrases.meaning: The muzzles joined the line behind the target; they must join ahead of it.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Match its speed — don't let it catch you.
phrases.meaning: Move the gun at the target's speed so the gap does not shrink.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You're measuring it — trust the picture and pull.
phrases.meaning: The shooter is slowing down to check the gap; fire as soon as the picture is right.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Come from behind, through the bird, and shoot as you see daylight.
phrases.meaning: Start behind the target, swing through it and fire as a gap appears in front.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Butt, belly, beak, bang.
phrases.meaning: Memory aid: tail, body, front of the target, then fire.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You slowed down as you got to it.
phrases.meaning: The gun lost speed when it reached the target, so the shot went behind.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Brush it out and keep going.
phrases.meaning: Swing through the target as if wiping it out of the sky, without stopping.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: On it, with it, pull away, shoot.
phrases.meaning: Join the target, track it, accelerate ahead, fire.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Touch it and go.
phrases.meaning: Meet the target with the muzzles and immediately start pulling ahead.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You rode it too long.
phrases.meaning: The shooter tracked the target for too long before pulling away and lost the line or the moment.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Mount on it and push out a bit more.
phrases.meaning: Mount onto the target, then pull a little further ahead before firing.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You're ambushing it — keep the gun moving with the target.
phrases.meaning: The shooter is waiting at a point; the coach wants a moving method here.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Ambush this one in the gap.
phrases.meaning: Deliberately wait at the opening and fire just before the target reaches your point, so it flies into the shot.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Don't think about the lead, just look at the bird and let the gun go to it.
phrases.meaning: Shoot instinctively: focus on the target and let the hands follow.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Hold right on the break point and just collapse onto it.
phrases.meaning: Put the muzzles almost at the break point and make only a tiny move as the battue arrives.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Behind, give it more.
phrases.meaning: The shot passed behind the clay; increase the lead.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Just over the top, it was already dropping.
phrases.meaning: The shot went above because the clay was falling; shoot lower and in front.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: In front this time, good, now a touch less.
phrases.meaning: Too much lead, but the gun was moving; reduce the lead slightly.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You just chipped it, a little more in front.
phrases.meaning: Hit on the edge of the pattern; a bit more lead centres it.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Smoked it! Same again.
phrases.meaning: A perfect centred hit (slang, not the rules' 'smoke'); repeat exactly.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Behind, but you stopped, so don't just add lead.
phrases.meaning: The cause is a stopped gun; more lead alone will not help.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You lifted your head, that's why it went over.
phrases.meaning: The cheek left the stock, so the shot went above the clay.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Keep the gun moving, you stopped on it.
phrases.meaning: The swing halted at the shot; continue moving through and after it.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You checked just before the shot, commit to it.
phrases.meaning: A brief hesitation before firing; decide and shoot without slowing.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Stop aiming, look at the bird and let the gun go.
phrases.meaning: Criticism: the shooter is pointing like a rifle; focus on the target and swing freely.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You rode it too long, take it earlier.
phrases.meaning: The shooter followed the clay too long; break it sooner.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Stay in the gun.
phrases.meaning: Keep the cheek on the stock until after the shot.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Bring the gun to your face, not your face to the gun.
phrases.meaning: Lift the stock to the cheek; do not lower the head to the stock.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Move, mount, shoot, all in one.
phrases.meaning: Start moving with the target, finish the mount as you fire, in one flowing action.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You canted the gun, keep it level.
phrases.meaning: The gun was tilted sideways at the shot.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Mount on the line.
phrases.meaning: The gun should come up already on the target's path.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Pre-mount this one, just for practice.
phrases.meaning: Training drill with the gun already at the shoulder; not allowed in a Sporting™ competition.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Eyes first to the second bird, then the gun.
phrases.meaning: Find the second target with the eyes before moving the gun.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Let the gun recover, then go to the second.
phrases.meaning: After the recoil, settle gun and cheek before the second shot.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Take the dropping one first.
phrases.meaning: Shoot first the target that will disappear or fall soonest.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Don't watch the first one break.
phrases.meaning: Move the eyes on to the second target at once.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You went for the wrong one first, stick to the plan.
phrases.meaning: The shooter changed the planned order of a pair whose order is free; a technique remark, not a rule breach.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Front edge.
phrases.meaning: Look at the front edge of the target, not at the whole clay or the gun.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Stay on the line.
phrases.meaning: Keep the gun moving along the target's flight line.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Finish it.
phrases.meaning: Keep the gun moving after the shot; complete the follow-through.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Smooth.
phrases.meaning: Move the gun calmly and evenly, without a jerk.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Gun down, please.
phrases.meaning: Referee: bring the stock below the vest line before calling.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Your stock was above the line. This is a warning.
phrases.meaning: First gun-position offence: verbal warning with a yellow card.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Don't mount before the target appears.
phrases.meaning: The gun may come up only once the target is visible.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Red card, zero.
phrases.meaning: A repeat offence on the same layout; the single is lost.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Butt under the tape until you see the target.
phrases.meaning: Sporting™ gun-down rule: the stock stays below the vest line until the target appears.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: No marker needed here — it's Compak.
phrases.meaning: Compak® Sporting has no vest-line requirement.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Gun up or down, your choice here.
phrases.meaning: Coach: in Compak® Sporting the gun position at the call is free.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Shooter number twenty-three!
phrases.meaning: Referee calling a missing shooter (three times within a minute).

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Watch your time.
phrases.meaning: Reminder of the 15-second limit between targets.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Over fifteen seconds. This is a warning.
phrases.meaning: First time over the limit: warning; next time a penalty.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Glasses on, or you can't shoot.
phrases.meaning: Without eye protection the shooter is treated as absent.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Ten seconds, call your target.
phrases.meaning: Reminder of the 10-second limit to call.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Warning: time.
phrases.meaning: First time over 10 seconds; noted on the score sheet.

phrases.speaker: shooter
phrases.en: Show me the targets, please.
phrases.meaning: Shooter to referee: start the presentation.

phrases.speaker: shooter
phrases.en: Again, please, B only.
phrases.meaning: Request to repeat one target of the menu.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Guns open during the show.
phrases.meaning: Referee: open and unload until the referee allows closing.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Watch where it turns.
phrases.meaning: Coach in training: notice the point where the clay changes direction or shape.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Start! / Competition!
phrases.meaning: Referee: the presentation is over and scored shooting begins.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Dead — only a chip, but it counts.
phrases.meaning: A small visible piece broke off, so it is a hit.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Lost — you were just behind it.
phrases.meaning: A miss; the shot went behind the target.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Don't argue with me later — say it now, before you call.
phrases.meaning: An objection must be made at once; calling the next target accepts the ruling.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Stay there, don't open the gun.
phrases.meaning: Referee: wait for the inspection; opening first costs the target.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Let me see the gun.
phrases.meaning: The referee examines the gun or cartridge.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Malfunction. No Bird, first warning.
phrases.meaning: First incident in the round: the target is repeated.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Second malfunction this round. Zero.
phrases.meaning: No repeat this time; the target is lost.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Don't move, keep the gun closed.
phrases.meaning: Referee: wait for the inspection after a failure.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: First malfunction. Yellow card, No Bird.
phrases.meaning: First incident of this type in the round; the target is thrown again.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: You have two minutes.
phrases.meaning: Time to repair or replace the gun.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Only the second shot counts on this one.
phrases.meaning: Repeat after a second-cartridge failure: miss with the first shot on purpose.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Report pair: the second comes on your shot.
phrases.meaning: Coach: the second target is released by the shot at the first.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: On the rafale, take either one first.
phrases.meaning: Coach: in a rafale double the order is free.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: One and one.
phrases.meaning: Referee: both targets of the double are hits.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: No Bird, repeat the double.
phrases.meaning: Irregular target; the double is thrown again.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: One shot per bird on the pairs here.
phrases.meaning: Coach: in Compak® Sporting each target of a double gets only one cartridge.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Both with one shot. No Bird, shoot the double again.
phrases.meaning: Referee on a simultaneous double: nothing scored, repeat.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Choose your order on the show.
phrases.meaning: Coach: decide which simultaneous target to take first while watching the presentation.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Zero, zero.
phrases.meaning: Referee: neither target of the double is scored.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Warning — your stock was above the line.
phrases.meaning: Sporting™: the gun was too high before the target appeared; next time on this layout it costs the target.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: That’s a yellow card.
phrases.meaning: An official first warning; it is recorded.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Red card — the target is zero.
phrases.meaning: A repeated offence on the stand: the target is scored as lost.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: You’re over time.
phrases.meaning: The shooter took longer than allowed (in Sporting™ 15 s between targets, in Compak® Sporting 10 s to call).

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Sir, please leave the shooting area.
phrases.meaning: The referee is removing someone, for example a person caught coaching.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: No coaching on the stand.
phrases.meaning: Referee warning: coaching is forbidden in competition.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Ears and eyes on before you walk up.
phrases.meaning: Put on hearing protection and glasses before approaching the stand.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Number on your back, please.
phrases.meaning: Referee: the competition number must be fully visible on the back.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Ears and eyes on.
phrases.meaning: Put on hearing protection and glasses before the station.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You’re in squad twelve, starting on layout five at nine-thirty.
phrases.meaning: Squad number, start layout and start time.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Check your card before you leave the stand.
phrases.meaning: Sporting™: make sure the referee recorded your score correctly now; later it is too late.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Twenty-two in the first round is fine — seven more to go.
phrases.meaning: 22 out of 25 in the first round; seven rounds remain in a 200-target event.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Stay close — if it’s a tie, you shoot within fifteen minutes of the call.
phrases.meaning: A shooter who may be in a shoot-off must be ready soon after being called.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Check your card before you leave the stand.
phrases.meaning: Sporting™: look at your marks now; later objections are not accepted.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Sign here, please.
phrases.meaning: Compak® Sporting: signing confirms the score; refusing means losing the right to complain.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Twenty-three — you dropped two.
phrases.meaning: Score 23 of 25; two targets were lost.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Which category are you shooting in?
phrases.meaning: Asked at registration: Junior, Lady, Men, Senior, Veteran or Master.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: He’s a Senior now.
phrases.meaning: He is in the 56–65 group this season.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: She won the Lady category and was fourth overall.
phrases.meaning: First among ladies, fourth in the open ranking.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: There’s a shoot-off for Veteran bronze.
phrases.meaning: Compak® Sporting (or a Sporting™ event whose programme has category shoot-offs): two or more Veterans are tied for third in their category.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: There’s a tie for third — shoot-off in fifteen minutes.
phrases.meaning: Be at the named layout and ready to shoot within fifteen minutes.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Sudden death: first zero is out.
phrases.meaning: After the 25-target shoot-off, the first shooter to miss (with an equal number of targets shot) is eliminated.

phrases.speaker: shooter
phrases.en: Protest! The target was broken before I fired.
phrases.meaning: The shooter formally challenges the ruling and gives the reason (here: a broken target was thrown).

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: I’m certain — the decision stands.
phrases.meaning: The referee confirms; the ruling is final.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Did anyone see a piece come off?
phrases.meaning: The referee is in doubt and asks the squad for advice only; the referee still decides.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: You can take it to the jury in writing, with the deposit.
phrases.meaning: This decision is appealable; a written appeal and a deposit are needed.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Please carry on shooting.
phrases.meaning: The ruling is final; resume now or it becomes a refusal to comply.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Tell her she’s lifting her head on the second bird.
phrases.meaning: Training: pass it on fully when the gun is open.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Quick — tell him to give the crosser more.
phrases.meaning: Competition: this is coaching. Decline politely; do not pass it on.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Who are you with?
phrases.meaning: The referee asks why you are near the stand; introduce yourself and your role.

phrases.speaker: shooter
phrases.en: Ask the referee if I can still change chokes.
phrases.meaning: A procedural question to the referee: you may interpret it.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Stand right behind me.
phrases.meaning: Behind the coach and the shooter, out of the swing.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Head on the stock — just whisper it to him, I’ll keep going.
phrases.meaning: Switch to chuchotage and pass the cue on quietly; the coach will not pause. With passive ear defenders, wait until the gun is open.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: When I do this — hands apart — it means more in front.
phrases.meaning: The coach explains a hand signal; translate it once for the group.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Wait — let him finish the pair.
phrases.meaning: Hold the advice until the gun is open again.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: You may load.
phrases.meaning: The referee allows shooting to start: put cartridges in now, gun pointing down the range.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: No bird!
phrases.meaning: That target does not count; do not shoot at it. It will be thrown again.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Lost.
phrases.meaning: The referee scored the target as a miss (zero).

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Dead. / Good.
phrases.meaning: The target is a hit (one).

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Guns open, please — we’re showing the targets.
phrases.meaning: Everyone opens and unloads; the referee will throw the targets for viewing.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Start. / Competition.
phrases.meaning: Compak® Sporting: viewing is over, the round counts from now.

phrases.speaker: shooter
phrases.en: Pull!
phrases.meaning: The call: release the target now. Say it short and clear, the same way each time.

phrases.speaker: shooter
phrases.en: I think I was behind it.
phrases.meaning: You tell the coach where you think the shot went: behind the target.

phrases.speaker: shooter
phrases.en: I saw it late.
phrases.meaning: You picked up the target late; this changes the coach’s advice, so say it.

phrases.speaker: shooter
phrases.en: Can I see that one again, please?
phrases.meaning: In training: ask to see the target again. In competition only where the rules allow it.

phrases.speaker: shooter
phrases.en: Can you show me with your hands?
phrases.meaning: Ask the coach to show the lead or the line with a gesture; useful when words are hard.

phrases.speaker: shooter
phrases.en: Sorry, could you say that again, slowly?
phrases.meaning: You did not understand the coach or the referee: ask for a slow repeat instead of guessing.

phrases.speaker: shooter
phrases.en: Protest!
phrases.meaning: With a raised hand, at once, on the stand: you formally disagree with the decision.

phrases.speaker: shooter
phrases.en: I saw a piece come off.
phrases.meaning: The reason for your protest: a visible piece broke off, so you think it was a hit.

phrases.speaker: shooter
phrases.en: Was that a no bird?
phrases.meaning: A calm question when the target looked irregular or came late. Accept the answer.

phrases.speaker: shooter
phrases.en: Morning, all — good luck today.
phrases.meaning: A greeting to the referee and the squad at the start of the round.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Where did it go?
phrases.meaning: The coach asks where the shooter thinks the shot went; a teaching question.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: What did you see?
phrases.meaning: Describe the picture at the moment of the shot.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: More.
phrases.meaning: In context it often means “more lead”; if unsure, ask one word: “Lead?”

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Good, same again.
phrases.meaning: Repeat exactly what you just did.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Trust it, commit to it.
phrases.meaning: Stop hesitating; decide and fire.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Bad luck.
phrases.meaning: Sympathy after a miss; not a complaint about the referee.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Head!
phrases.meaning: Your head came off the stock: keep your cheek down on it through the shot.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Where did you first see it clearly?
phrases.meaning: The coach wants your pick-up point: the place where your eyes first found the target sharply.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Give it four foot.
phrases.meaning: Give the lead the coach calls “four feet”; it describes his picture, so keep his number and unit.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Half a bird more.
phrases.meaning: Add half a target’s width to the lead picture.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Double it.
phrases.meaning: Make the lead picture twice as big as last time.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Same lead, just keep it moving.
phrases.meaning: The lead was right; the miss came from stopping the gun.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: That one goes right to left. You were at two o’clock: a touch lower and more in front.
phrases.meaning: On a target flying right to left, the shot cloud (the pattern) went above and behind it, at two o’clock on the target. Shoot slightly lower and give a little more lead.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: A barrel’s width in front.
phrases.meaning: Keep a gap the width of the barrel, as seen at the muzzle, ahead of the target.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: One target at a time.
phrases.meaning: Forget the score and the last target: give this one target your full attention.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Read the target.
phrases.meaning: Before you shoot, work out its line, speed and distance, and where it is easiest to break.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Have a plan and commit to it.
phrases.meaning: Decide your points and the order while the targets are shown (in Compak® Sporting, often while watching the shooters before you), then shoot that plan without changing it mid-shot.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Commit to your break point.
phrases.meaning: Shoot where you planned; do not let the shot drift further along the line.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Soft eyes, then hard focus.
phrases.meaning: Look loosely at the pick-up area; once the target appears, lock your eyes sharply on it.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Front edge.
phrases.meaning: Look at the leading edge of the target, not at the whole clay or at the gun.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Stare it to death.
phrases.meaning: Keep an intense, unbroken focus on the target until the shot.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Don’t look at the barrel.
phrases.meaning: Your eyes stay on the target; the gun stays at the edge of your vision.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Trust it.
phrases.meaning: Stop checking the lead; let your trained movement do the work.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Let it happen.
phrases.meaning: Do not force or steer the shot; let the swing and the shot come as you trained them.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: See it, shoot it.
phrases.meaning: When the picture is right, fire without second-guessing.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Don’t ride it.
phrases.meaning: Do not follow the target too long trying to be sure; shoot when the picture is right.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Keep the gun moving.
phrases.meaning: No pause at the trigger: the swing goes on through the shot.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Two separate shots.
phrases.meaning: A pair is two targets, each with its own plan and its own break point.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Don’t chase the first one.
phrases.meaning: After the first shot, move your eyes to the second target instead of watching the first one break.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Let it go.
phrases.meaning: Accept the miss and stop thinking about it; the next target matters now.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Reset.
phrases.meaning: Do your short routine after the shot and start the next target fresh.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Process, not outcome.
phrases.meaning: Think about doing your routine well, not about the score.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Control the controllables.
phrases.meaning: Spend your attention on what you can change, such as your routine and effort, not on the weather, the referee or the squad.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Play your own game.
phrases.meaning: Shoot your own plan and pace; do not copy the shooter before you.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Smoked it!
phrases.meaning: Perfect hit, the target turned to dust. Not the rules’ “smoke only”.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Only dust — zero.
phrases.meaning: Referee: no visible piece came off, so it is a miss.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Just a chip, but it’s dead.
phrases.meaning: A small visible piece broke off: it counts as a hit.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Break your gun.
phrases.meaning: Open the gun. Nothing to do with breaking it.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Step into the peg.
phrases.meaning: Stand on the marked shooting spot.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: The second one’s on report.
phrases.meaning: The second target is released by the sound of your first shot.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Give it three feet.
phrases.meaning: The lead picture the coach wants; a perceived gap, not a measured distance.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Half that.
phrases.meaning: Use half of the previous lead.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Pick it up at eleven o’clock.
phrases.meaning: Look for the target slightly left of straight ahead.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: It’s about forty yards out.
phrases.meaning: The target is roughly 37 metres away.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Put a nine in the bottom barrel.
phrases.meaning: Put a No. 9 shot cartridge (about 2 mm) in the lower barrel, which usually fires first.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Pre-mount this one for now.
phrases.meaning: Training drill: start with the gun in the shoulder. Not allowed in FITASC Sporting™ competition.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: It’s a true pair.
phrases.meaning: Both targets leave at the same time (FITASC: simultaneous double).

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Following pair off the left trap.
phrases.meaning: Two targets from the same trap one after the other (FITASC: rafale).

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Let’s see a show pair.
phrases.meaning: Throw the pair once so everyone can watch it before shooting.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: He’s AA class and won HOA last year.
phrases.meaning: A high national skill class, and overall winner of the event.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Behind.
phrases.meaning: The shot passed behind the target (too little lead or a stopped gun; the coach will say which).

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: In front.
phrases.meaning: The shot passed in front of the target.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Over.
phrases.meaning: The shot passed above the target.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Under.
phrases.meaning: The shot passed below the target.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: A bit more.
phrases.meaning: Add a little more lead.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Less.
phrases.meaning: Give less lead.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Hold point.
phrases.meaning: Where the muzzles wait when you call.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Pick-up point.
phrases.meaning: Where your eyes first see the target clearly.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Break point.
phrases.meaning: Where you plan to break the target.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Mount.
phrases.meaning: Bring the gun up to your cheek and shoulder.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Finish it.
phrases.meaning: Keep the gun moving after the shot (follow-through).

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Head down.
phrases.meaning: Keep your cheek on the stock.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Check your feet.
phrases.meaning: Set your stance towards the break point.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Wait for it.
phrases.meaning: Do not move the gun yet: let the target come to your hold point.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Show me where you saw it.
phrases.meaning: Point to the place where you first saw the target clearly.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Same again.
phrases.meaning: Repeat exactly what you just did.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Open the gun.
phrases.meaning: Open the gun now: you will talk or wait.

phrases.speaker: shooter
phrases.en: Slower, please.
phrases.meaning: Ask the coach to speak more slowly.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Morning, everyone. Before we load anything, a quick safety briefing.
phrases.meaning: Start of the session; interpret the briefing consecutively and completely.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Guns stay open until you’re on the stand and I say “load”.
phrases.meaning: No closed guns off the stand; loading only on the coach’s word.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Point at my nose, both eyes open. Now close your left eye.
phrases.meaning: Eye-dominance check: if the finger jumps, the right eye is not the master eye.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Front foot pointing at the break point, weight forward.
phrases.meaning: Stance: set the feet for where the target will be broken; lean slightly forward.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Gun down, stock under the line. Mount only when you see it.
phrases.meaning: Sporting™ ready position: the mount starts only after the target appears; in Compak® Sporting the position at the call is free.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Watch this one. Where do you first see it clearly?
phrases.meaning: The coach is setting the pick-up point.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Hold your muzzles about halfway back, just under the line.
phrases.meaning: Hold point between pick-up and break point, slightly below the target’s path.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Behind it. Give it more.
phrases.meaning: The shot passed behind the target: more lead.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Call it three feet — that’s the picture you want.
phrases.meaning: The gap the coach wants the shooter to see at the shot. “Three feet” describes how it looks, not a measured distance, so keep the unit.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Over the top. You lifted your head — stay in the gun.
phrases.meaning: Miss above, caused by the cheek leaving the stock (head lift).

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Smoked it! Same again.
phrases.meaning: Perfect hit; repeat exactly what you did.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You stopped the gun. Keep it moving through the shot.
phrases.meaning: Miss behind because the swing stopped (stopping the gun); follow through.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Next is a report pair: crosser first, then the rabbit.
phrases.meaning: A double on report: the rabbit is released by the sound of the shot at the crosser.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Eyes first, then the gun.
phrases.meaning: On the second target, find it with the eyes before moving the muzzles.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Keep the muzzles under the rabbit.
phrases.meaning: Keep the muzzles below the rabbit: if it bounces up, it hops into the shot instead of over it.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Change to quarter and half for this stand.
phrases.meaning: Fit 1/4 and 1/2 chokes (open, then a little tighter).

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Let’s call it a day. Three things for tomorrow: feet, head, follow-through.
phrases.meaning: End of session; the coach sums up — write these down for the guest.
